findings.title: Global canManage() grants manage rights to admins holding only the VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Since hasPermission returns true if ANY of the listed scopes is granted, an admin who only has the `view` scope on the all-groups resource passes canManage(). This method backs `auth.groups().requireManage()`, which guards group creation (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup) and other write paths, so a view-only fine-grained admin can create/modify top-level groups — a privilege escalation. The same pattern does not exist for users (UserPermissions.canManage() only checks MANAGE_SCOPE). The javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() ("permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") appears to have replicated this mistake rather than describing intended behavior. It should only accept the MANAGE scope, and a negative test (view-only all-groups permission must not allow group creation) should be added.

findings.title: NPE in hasPermission when the group resource and the all-groups resource are both missing
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null (no per-group resource exists), the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null when the resource server is not the admin-permissions client or admin permissions are not enabled, and can also simply find no 'Groups' type resource. In that case `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` and the subsequent `resource.getScopes()` on line 152 will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning false. The null case must be handled (return false), as done implicitly by the early null checks in the V1 GroupPermissions.hasPermission.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Groups handling, so group permission resources display null names
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases the USERS resource type (returning "All users" or the username) but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. For group policies, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, and group resources created via getOrCreateResource never set a display name (only name = group id). Any UI/logic that renders policy resources for the admin-permissions client will therefore show a raw group id or null instead of a human-readable group name. A resolveGroup-based branch (mirroring the Users handling) is needed.

findings.title: No negative test that a VIEW-only all-groups permission does not grant manage operations
findings.body: testManageAllGroups only verifies that MANAGE on all-groups enables group creation/update, but there is no test asserting that an admin holding only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is still forbidden from creating or updating groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup / GroupResource.updateGroup). Because GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope in its fallback (see separate finding), this exact regression is currently unguarded by the test suite; adding such a negative test would catch it.
